decisions.reason: As a very recent launch in a strategic particle-therapy niche, its value is still uncertain but the option should be kept open despite the delayed US release because it fits the firm's core QA portfolio and can still reveal market potential.

This small-volume ionization chamber is a close-to-core extension with likely modest carrying cost, so management would keep it on the market while learning about adoption rather than abandon it after only one year.
Because it is another newly launched chamber in the firm's established dosimetry domain, the firm would treat it as a low-cost option and retain it until clearer sales and user feedback emerge.
A standard clinical ionization chamber sits squarely in the firm's established business, so early uncertainty is not enough to justify withdrawal and the product is likely to be kept.
Although more specialized for relative dosimetry, it still complements the firm's measurement ecosystem and should remain available while the firm tests demand and cross-selling potential.
